courses.description: Introduces the basic concepts, terminology, etiology, and characteristics of pathological processes.

courses.title: Healthcare Information Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches basic concepts of microcomputer software (to include operating systems, word processing, spreadsheets, and database applications. Focuses on microcomputer applications and information systems in the Healthcare environment. Provides a working introduction to electronic health information systems for allied health, teaching students how the adoption of electronic health records affects them as future healthcare professionals.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Health Information Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on health data collection, storage, retrieval and reporting systems, with emphasis on the role of the computer in accomplishing these functions. Part I of II.

courses.title: Reimbursement Issues in Medical Practice Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces major reimbursement systems in the United States. Focuses on prospective payment systems, managed care, and documentation necessary for appropriate reimbursement. Emphasizes management of practice to avoid fraud.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college. Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Health Record Documentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the legal requirements associated with health record documentation. Emphasizes the policies and procedures concerning the protection of the confidentiality of patient's health records.

courses.title: Health Data Classification Systems I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the current classification systems used in the healthcare industry. Introduces the professional standards for coding and reporting of inpatient/outpatient diagnostic codes as well as inpatient procedures. Utilizes standards in identifying and accurately assigning codes to diseases and procedures as they relate to statistical research and healthcare financing.

courses.title: Health Data Classification Systems II: CPT
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on procedure classification using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT). This system is currently utilized for collecting health data for the purposes of statistical research and financial reporting.

courses.title: Health Data Classifications Systems III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Integrates and applies knowledge with hands-on skill practice in coding. Reinforces medical terminology, anatomy, and coding guidelines for International Classification of Diseases (ICD) and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT). Introduces the student to the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) coding guidelines. Promotes critical thinking related to coding quality, fraud, and abuse.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college. Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Pre-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from ancient times to 1600 CE. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Western Civilizations Post-1600 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the development of western civilization from 1600 CE to the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Pre-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Europe from antiquity to approximately 1500. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: World Civilizations Post-1500 CE
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas from approximately 1500 CE through the present. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History to 1877
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from its origins to 1877. Includes the European exploration, development of the American colonies and their institutions, the Revolution, major political, social and economic developments, geographical expansion, the Civil War, and Reconstruction. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: United States History Since 1865
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the history of the United States from 1865 to present. Includes major political, social and economic developments since 1865, overseas expansion, the two world wars, the Cold War and the post-Cold War era. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: African-American History I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of African Americans from their African origins to 1876.

courses.title: African-American History II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the history of black Americans from their African origins to the present. Part II of II.

courses.title: History of African Civilization
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines major social, economic, political and religious developments across the African continent from earliest times to the present. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: History of Virginia
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the cultural, economic, political, and religious history of Virginia from pre-contact to the present. Includes diverse perspectives to emphasize the significant contributions different groups of people (African Americans, Indigenous Peoples, European-Americans, Women) made to the history of Virginia, the colonies, and the United States.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Provides training in coordinated mouth-to-mouth artificial ventilation and chest compression, choking, life-threatening emergencies, and sudden illness. Equivalent to EMS 100 .

courses.title: First Aid and Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and techniques of safety and first aid.

courses.title: Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of health and dimensions of wellness through exploration of a variety of personal health topics. Identifies factors that affect the health status of individuals in addition to health promotion and disease prevention at the personal and community level.

courses.title: Introduction to Personal and Community Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Introduces and focuses on the principles of personal and community health.

courses.title: Substance Abuse: Prevention and Treatment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the use and abuse of drugs in contemporary society with emphasis upon sociological, physiological, and psychological effects of drugs.

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of medical abbreviations and terms. Includes the study of prefixes, suffixes, word stems and technical terms with emphasis on proper spelling, pronunciation and usage.

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of various forms of physical activity and how they promote human health. Examines the study of physical activity from the perspectives of professional practice, scholarly study and experience. Provides a broad overview of the history, scientific principles, methodologies, and research among the major subdisciplines to prepare students for further study in kinesiology and health sciences. Explores current issues, future directions, certifications, professional associations, and career opportunities.

courses.title: Personal Stress Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of stress and explores its physical, psychological and social effects. Includes the relationships among stress and change, self-evaluation, sources of stress, and ways to develop current coping skills for handling stress. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of public health systems in the United States and globally with an emphasis on core functions, essential services and health determinants. Explores the history, core areas and current trends within public health as well as how public health affects individuals and populations. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: Principles of Nutrition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic concepts of nutrition and its impact on personal wellness. Emphasizes an evidence-based approach to various topics, such as the nutrient components of food, the components of a healthy eating pattern, and the relationship between diet and health. Provides a behavioral approach to nutrient guidelines for the development and maintenance of optimum wellness. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through documented written reports.

courses.title: Global Health Perspectives
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines global health theories, concepts, issues and prevention efforts. Analyzes the complex relationship between economics, environment, culture and values in addressing health disparities and access to healthcare around the globe. Explores health inequities across the globe by using contemporary, evidence-based topics.

courses.title: Basic Pharmacy II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the basics of general pharmacy, reading prescriptions, symbols, packages, pharmacy calculations. Teaches measuring compounds of drugs, dosage forms, drug laws, and drug classifications. Part II of II.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces human service agencies, roles and careers. Presents an historical perspective of the field as it relates to human services today. Additional topics include values clarification and needs of target populations.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills needed to function in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in attending, listening and responding. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement.

courses.title: Basic Counseling Skills II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per work.
courses.description: Expands the development of counseling skills needed to function effectively in a helping relationship. Emphasizes skills in responding, personalizing, summarizing and initiating. Clarifies personal skill strengths, deficits and goals for skill improvement. Develops plans for achieving personal and program goals.

courses.title: Group Dynamics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the stages of group development, group dynamics, the role of the leader in a group, and recognition of the various types of group processes. Discusses models of group dynamics that occur as a result of group membership dynamics.

courses.title: Group Dynamics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines group dynamics, group leadership, group cohesion, transference and group helping through experiential involvement in group facilitating and leadership. Increases group skills through active classroom participation in group experiences.

courses.title: Addiction and Prevention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the impact of drugs and addiction on individuals and their families. Explores the myths about various drugs and their benefit or lack of benefit.

courses.title: Functional Family Intervention
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of functions and dysfunctions within the family. Emphasizes the development of effective skills through an interpersonal/interactional approach to family intervention.

courses.title: Helping Across Cultures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an historical overview of selected cultural and racial groups. Promotes understanding of group differences and the impact on counseling services.

courses.title: The Helper As a Change Agent
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the following skills for implementing alternative models of change and influence: action research, problem- solving, consultation, workshop development, and outreach and advocacy for diverse client populations.

courses.title: Gerontology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the process of aging; its implications in relation to health, recreation, education, transportation, meaningful work or activity, and to community resources. Emphasizes experiencing the aging process, facilitating retirement, and application of the helping relationship to work with older adults.

courses.title: Case Management and Substance Abuse
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the process for interviewing substance abuse clients. Includes intake, assessment, handling denial, and ending the interview. Teaches skills for writing short-term goals and treatment plans with emphasis on accountability. Examines various reporting devices.

courses.title: Substance Abuse Counseling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of the skills of guidance of clients and those associated with being an advocate. Examines the dynamics of the client/counselor relationship in developing treatment plans and empowerment skills.

courses.title: Counseling Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies major counseling theories, their contributions and limitations, and the application of each to a counseling interaction. Students develop their own personal counseling theory.

courses.title: Treatment Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the services and facilities established for the purpose of treating addictions. Focuses on treatment therapy models and ethical standards related to addiction-disease theory.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Principles of Culinary Arts I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental principles of food preparation and basic culinary procedures. Stresses the use of proper culinary procedures combined with food science, proper sanitation, standards of quality for food items that are made, and proper use and care of kitchen equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Applied Mathematics for the Food Service Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Examines comprehensive mathematical skills necessary for various careers in the food service industry. Includes conversions, scaling, yield percent's, purchasing and portioning, recipe costing, and kitchen ratios.

courses.title: Food Service Managers Sanitation Certification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents an accelerated survey of principles and applications of sanitary food service, designed to promote the skills of managers in food service establishments licensed by the Commonwealth of Virginia. (Upon successful completion of the course, a certificate of achievement is awarded by the Educational Foundation of the National Restaurant Association and the student's name is entered in the Foundation Registry.)

courses.title: Applied Nutrition for Food Service Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-5 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes application of skill sets for understanding, reviewing, revising, scaling, and preparing existing recipes and the creation of new recipes with a focus on healthy cooking techniques, alternative products, and critical thinking.

courses.title: Principles of Baking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of breads, pastries, baked desserts, candies, frozen confections, and sugar work. Applies scientific principles and techniques of baking. Promotes the knowledge/skills required to prepare baked items, pastries and confections.

courses.title: Storeroom Operations and Inventory Management Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 5 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores through laboratory activities the flow of foods, beverages, and supplies in food service establishments, including product identification, purchasing, receiving, storage, measuring, data entry systems, inventory, and evaluation through discussion and demonstration.

courses.title: Introduction to Hospitality Industry Computer Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 -3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 -5 hours per week.
courses.description: Familiarizes students with computerized information technology to manage information, support decision-making and analysis, improve processes, increase productivity and enhance customer service in the hospitality industry.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: International Cuisine
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of cultural differences and similarities and the preparation of the food specialties of the major geographical areas of the world. Focuses on emerging cuisines as they become popular.

courses.title: American Regional Cuisine
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the distinct regional cooking styles of America and its neighbors. Emphasizes the indigenous ingredients as well as the cultural aspect of each region's cooking style. Includes the preparation of the various regional foods.

courses.title: Fruit, Vegetable, and Starch Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of fruits, vegetables, grains, cereals, legumes and farinaceous products. Promotes the knowledge/skills necessary to prepare menu items from fruits, vegetables, and their byproducts, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Stock, Soup, and Sauce Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Instructs the student in the preparation of stocks, soups, and sauces. Promotes the knowledge/skills to prepare stocks, soups, and sauces, and to select appropriate uses as meal components.

courses.title: Meat, Seafood and Poultry Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides the study and preparation of meat, poultry, shellfish, fish, and game. Promotes the knowledge/skills required to select appropriate use of these foods as meal components.

courses.title: Leadership and Kitchen Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents advanced principles of the foodservice industry by exploring modern leadership techniques, effective management routines, characteristics of strong leadership, employee selection and hiring, performance reviews, and career development.

courses.title: Current Issues & Environmental Responsibilities in the Hospitality Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Total 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies aspects of the evolving hospitality industry, including the collective impact of environmental stewardship and sustainability, local sourcing of products and ingredients, greening of hospitality businesses, cost-benefit analyses of sustainability decisions, and ethical questions related to these topics. Environmental Sustainability Designation: Course content related to the study of sustainable development.

courses.title: Food and Beverage Cost Control I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents methods of pre-cost and pre-control as applied to the menu, purchasing, receiving, storing, issuing, production, sales and service which result in achievement of an operation's profit potential. Emphasizes both manual and computerized approaches. Part I of II.

courses.title: Hospitality Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies legal principles governing hospitality operations. Includes applications of common law and statutory decisions, discussion of legal theory, and regulations governing management of hospitality enterprise.

courses.title: Artisan Breads
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an integrated study of both classical and modern baking methods. Focuses on craft baking using simple ingredients to create superior products.

courses.title: Chocolate and Sugar Arts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on an integrated study of chocolate and sugar as used by the pastry artist to create candies, confections and showpieces.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Practical Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practical experience in landscape construction equipment operations and maintenance.

courses.title: Principles of Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces concepts of plant growth and development. Covers horticultural practices, crops and environmental factors affecting plant growth.

courses.title: Plant Propagation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of plant propagation. Examines commercial and home practices. Provides experience in techniques using seed-spores, cuttings, grafting, budding, layering and division.

courses.title: History of Garden Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the development of gardens as they chronicle the development of civilization. Introduces the periods, in both Europe and North America, beginning with settlement, on through industrial development, land and space utilization to current environmental concerns. Explores physical and cultural influences on garden design and utilization.

courses.title: Greenhouse Crop Production I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers commercial practices related to production of floriculture crops. Considers production requirements, environmental control and management, and cultural techniques.

courses.title: Chemicals in Horticulture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes basic chemical principles and their application to horticulture. Introduces principles of inorganic and organic chemicals. Studies chemical activities of insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, fertilizers, and growth regulators.

courses.title: Home Landscaping
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies current approaches to improving home landscapes. Emphasizes planning, proper implementation, and landscape maintenance.

courses.title: Horticultural Botany
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies taxonomy, anatomy, morphology, physiology, and genetics of plants as applied to identification, propagation and culture.

courses.title: Introduction to Sustainable Farming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Familiarizes students, through lecture and demonstration, with small-scale food production by gardening. Covers the basics of composting and organic vegetable gardening using sustainable farming methods.

courses.title: Four Season Food Production
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Familiarizes students with organic small-scale food production through lecture and demonstration. Includes seed saving, cover crops, and gardening planning.

courses.title: Training for Commercial Pesticide Application
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the principles and practices for safe pesticide usage as required by law in the state of Virginia. Prepares students for the official tests administered by VDACS (Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services).

courses.title: Hydroponics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the topic of water and nutrient relationships as they relate to soilless media for plant production. Examines plant/water relationships and optimum nutrition.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Landscape Plants I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part I of II.

courses.title: Landscape Plants II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies landscape use of plants. Considers ornamental value, growth habit, identification, and limitations. Part II of II.

courses.title: Soils
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches theoretical and practical aspects of soils and other growing media. Examines media components, chemical and physical properties, and soil organisms. Discusses management and conservation.

courses.title: Planting Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies landscape theory and principles of drawing to the planning of residential and small scale commercial landscape designs.

courses.title: Growing for Market
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: HRT 130 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Focuses on development of a marketing plan for sustainable farm items offered for sale to the public, retail and wholesale. Includes hands-on experience in double digging, planting, crop testing and utilization of compost.

courses.title: Complete Diet Farming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: HRT 130 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Considers sustainable farming methods by which food can be grown for personal or family consumption, emphasizing high nutritional yield in relatively small areas. Focuses on the development of a garden plan that includes vegetable and root crops and grains used for food and composting.

courses.title: Perennial Plants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Considers the perennial plants used in the landscape. Includes site selection and evaluation for perennial culture, perennial plant selection, perennial culture under various environmental conditions, taxonomic identification, and control of insects and diseases.

courses.title: Arboriculture
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the techniques of tree care. Covers surgery, pruning, insect and disease recognition and control, fertilization, cabling, and lightning rod installation.

courses.title: Introduction to Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for the composition of basic table arrangements. Includes the history of design styles, identification of flowers and green, identification and use of equipment, and conditioning and handling of flowers.

courses.title: Advanced Floral Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for composition of traditional floral designs and contemporary floral designs. Includes use of exotic florals to create arrangement styles such as Japanese, European and Williamsburg.

courses.title: Advanced Floral Design Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches skills required for the composition of large floral arrangements. Includes wedding, funeral and special occasion designs for the home as well as public areas. Includes use of dried and silk flowers for special occasions.

courses.title: Management of a Horticultural Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the business and selling practices which relate to wholesale and retail horticultural businesses including garden centers, greenhouses, nurseries, and flower shops. Examines planning and layout, suppliers, merchandising, maintenance, and display of horticultural items.

courses.title: Sustainable Landscape Practices
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Considers the theory and practical application of green infrastructure, sustainable landscape maintenance practices, regenerative landscapes, and stormwater best management practices (BMPs). Teaches the guiding principles of sustainable landscape design and development. Examines the social and economic benefits of well-designed and carefully maintained ecologically-sound urban and suburban landscapes.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Modern Humanities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the values and expression of ideas of selected western and non-western cultures from the 1300s until 1900s, integrating the visual arts, literature, religion, music and philosophy within the context of history. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Women and Gender Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Broadens understanding and awareness of women by exploring different cultural, historical, and gendered experiences of social groups throughout the world in relationship to such fields as art, literature, religion, philosophy, social sciences, and music. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Comparative Mythology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the cultural expressions of mythology. Considers selected mythologies representing diverse global culture, with emphasis on parallels and divergences in structure, purpose, and representation in literature and the arts. The assignments in this course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through properly cited and formatted written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Interpreting Foundations I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops fundamental skills of interpreting, including cognitive processes and intralingual language development in English and ASL. Reviews Process Models of interpreting, and uses one to analyze interpretations. Develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process. Part I of II.

courses.title: Interpreting Foundations I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops fundamental skills of interpreting, including cognitive processes and intralingual language development in English and ASL. Reviews Process Models of interpreting, and uses one to analyze interpretations. Develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process. Part II of II.

courses.title: Translation Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 105 .
courses.description: Further develops fundamental skills needed for the task of interpreting Targets comprehending source language (either ASL or English), transferring content into memory store (breaking from original form), restructuring into target language, maintaining message equivalence, conveying implicit and inferred information, and applying appropriate discourse structure. Review Process Model of interpreting, and uses it to analyze translations. Further develops feedback skills essential to the team interpreting process.

courses.title: Interpreting: An Introduction to the Profession
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic principles and practices of interpreting, focusing on the history of the profession, logistics of interpreting situations, regulatory and legislative issues, resources, and the Code of Ethics. Describes the state quality assurance screening and national certification exam systems, including test procedures.

courses.title: ASL-to-English Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Begins consecutively interpreting monologues from the source language (ASL) to the target language (English). Watch entire ASL monologues process them, analyze them, then choose appropriate English to match the message. Eventually interpret the monologue into English. Puts interpreting theory into practice in a lab environment. Conducts research in the field of interpretation. Develops team interpreting techniques. Interacts with consumers of ASL-English interpretation.

courses.title: English-to-ASL Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisite: INT 107 .
courses.description: Begins consecutively interpreting monologues from the source language (English) to the target language (ASL). Listen to entire English monologues, process them, analyze them, then choose appropriate ASL to match the message. Puts interpreting theory into practice in a lab environment. Conducts research into the field of interpretation. Develops team interpreting techniques. Encourages interaction with consumers of ASL-English interpretation.

courses.title: ASL-to English Interpretation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134 .
courses.description: Perform simultaneous interpretations of monologues in the source language (ASL) to the target language (English). Process an incoming ASL monologue while simultaneously producing an appropriate interpretation in English. Conduct research in the field of interpretation. Apply team interpreting techniques. Interact with consumers of interpretation.

courses.title: English-to-ASL Interpretation II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134 .
courses.description: Perform simultaneous interpretations of monologues in the source language (English) into the target language (ASL). Process an incoming English monologue while simultaneously producing an appropriate interpretation in ASL. Conduct research in the field of interpretation. Apply tem interpreting techniques. Interact with consumers of interpretation.

courses.title: Interpreting ASL in Safe Settings
courses.contact_hours: 2-3 Credits, Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 133 and INT 134
courses.description: Studies roles, responsibilities, and experiences involved in interpreting American Sign Language (ASL) in community and educational settings, including ethical and business practices. Analyzes the specific linguistic needs of the clients, managing the environment, and resolving ethical concerns for interpreters.

courses.title: Dialogic Interpretation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: INT 233 and INT 234 .
courses.description: Apply interpreting fundamentals. Interpret dialogs between spoken English and ASL users. Analyze interpretations by using a Process Model of Interpreting. Conduct research. Practice team interpreting skills in an interactive interpreting environment. Prepare for the interactive nature of standard interpreting evaluations.

courses.title: Interpreter Assessment Preparation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares student to sit for a specific interpreter assessment tool. Examines the contents of the various segments of the assessment tool. Provides an opportunity for the student to design and implement a specific individualized work plan based upon a diagnostic assessment of the student's interpretation product to improve all knowledge, skill and ability elements in order to meet or exceed the competency set for the selected interpreter assessment tool.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Web Page Design I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses a working knowledge of web site designs, construction, and management using HTML or XHTML. Includes headings, lists, links, images, image maps, tables, forms, and frames.

courses.title: Designing Web Page Graphics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the creation of digital graphics for web design. Includes basic design elements such as color and layout will be explored utilizing a computer graphics program(s).

courses.title: Database Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the student to Relational Database and Relational Database theory. Includes planning, defining and using a database; table design, linking, and normalization; types of databases, database description and definition.

courses.title: Structured Query Language
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates a working introduction to commands, functions and operators used in SQL for extracting data from standard databases.

courses.title: Web Page Design II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates advanced techniques in web site planning, design, usability, accessibility, advanced site management, and maintenance utilizing web editor software(s).

courses.title: Interactive Web Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides techniques in interactive design concepts to create cross-platform, low-bandwidth animations utilizing a vector based application. Emphasizes the importance of usability, accessibility, optimization and performance.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Spreadsheeting for Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a working knowledge of a commercial spreadsheet package to include design and development of a variety of worksheets, preparing graphs, working with database queries, macro writing, menu techniques, and decision analysis tools.

courses.title: Desktop Database Software
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Incorporates instruction in planning, defining, and using a database; performing queries; producing reports; working with multiple files; and concepts of database programming. Includes database concepts, principles of table design and table relationships, entering data, creating and using forms, using data from different sources, filtering, creating mailing labels.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital and Information Literacy and Computer Applications
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops understanding of digital and information literacy. Introduces basic computer concepts in hardware, software, cyber, cloud, database, and operating systems. Includes hands-on experience developing word processing, spreadsheet and presentation documents. Evaluates the reliability of sources. Covers creating a simple web page. Examines topics such as social, legal, and ethical issues. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to Network Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in networking media, physical and logical topologies, common networking standards and popular networking protocols. Emphasizes the TCP/IP protocol suite and related IP addressing schemes, including CIDR. Includes selected topics in network implementation, support and LAN/WAN connectivity.

courses.title: Microcomputer Operating Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches use of operating system utilities and multiple-level directory structures, creation of batch files, and configuration of microcomputer environments. May include a study of graphical user interfaces.

courses.title: Personal Computer Hardware and Troubleshooting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes specially designed instruction to give a student a basic knowledge of hardware and software configurations. Includes the installation of various peripheral devices as well as basic system hardware components.

courses.title: Linux System Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction on the installation, configuration and administration of the Linux operating system and emphasizes the use of Linux as a network client and workstation.

courses.title: Administration of Network Resources
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the management of local area network servers. Teaches proper structuring of security systems. Explains print queues, disk management, and other local area network (LAN) issues. Presents concerns and issues for the purchase and installation of hardware and software upgrades. Can be taught using any network operating system or a range of operating systems as a delivery tool.

courses.title: Virtual Infrastructure: Installation and Configuration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores concepts and capabilities of virtual architecture with a focus on the installation, configuration, and management of a virtual infrastructure, and Virtual Center. Covers fundamentals of virtual network design and implementation, fundamentals of storage area networks, virtual switching, virtual system management, and engineering for high availability.

courses.title: Cloud Computing: Infrastructure and Services
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on cloud infrastructure, deployment, security models, and the key considerations in migrating to cloud computing. Covers the technologies and processes required to build traditional, virtualized, and cloud data center environments, including computation, storage, networking, desktop and application virtualization, business continuity, security, and management.

courses.title: Network Security Basics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the basics of network security in depth. Includes security objectives, security architecture, security models and security layers; risk management, network security policy, and security training. Includes the five security keys, confidentiality integrity, availability, accountability and auditability.

courses.title: Network Attacks, Computer Crime and Hacking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Encompasses in-depth exploration of various methods for attacking and defending a network. Explores network security concepts from the viewpoint hackers and their attack methodologies. Includes topics about hackers, attacks, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) malicious code, computer crime and industrial espionage.

courses.title: Network Communication, Security and Authentication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers an in-depth exploration of various communication protocols with a concentration on TCP/IP. Explores communication protocols from the point of view of the hacker in order to highlight protocol weaknesses. Includes Internet architecture, routing, addressing, topology, fragmentation and protocol analysis, and the use of various utilities to explore TCP/IP.

courses.title: Internet/Intranet Firewalls and E-Commerce Security
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Gives an in-depth exploration of firewall, Web security, and e-commerce security. Explores firewall concepts, types, topology and the firewall's relationship to the TCP/IP protocol. Includes client/server architecture, the Web server, HTML and HTTP in relation to Web Security, and digital certification, D.509, and public key infrastructure (PKI).

courses.title: Computer Forensics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITN 106 , ITN 107 . Co-requisite: ITN 260 .
courses.description: Teaches computer forensic investigation techniques for collecting computer-related evidence at the physical layer from a variety of digital media (hard drives, compact flash and PDAs) and performing analysis at the file system layer. Credit will be given to ITN 275 or ITN 276 and ITN 277 , but not all three courses.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Software Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces principles and practices of software development. Includes instruction in critical thinking, problem solving skills, and essential programming logic in structured and object-oriented design using contemporary tools.

courses.title: C# Programming I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents instruction in fundamentals of object-oriented programming and design using C#. Emphasizes program construction, algorithm development, coding, debugging, and documentation of applications within the .NET framework.

courses.title: C# Programming II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses instruction in advanced object-oriented techniques using C# for application development. Emphasizes database connectivity and networking using the .NET Framework.

courses.title: Developing User Interfaces
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in the creation of computer application user interfaces that offer intuitive navigation and informative design for web, mobile, and desktop applications, and other technologies.

courses.title: Systems Analysis and Design
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on application of information technologies (IT) to system life cycle methodology, systems analysis, systems design, and system implementation practices. Covers methodologies related to identification of information requirements, feasibility in the areas of economic, technical and social requirements, and related issues are included in course content. Software applications may be used to enhance student skills.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to the Law and the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various areas of law in which a paralegal may be employed. Includes study of the court system (Virginia and federal); a brief overview of criminal law, torts, family law, evidence, the U.C.C., contracts, and ethics; the role of the paralegal; and other areas of interest.

courses.title: Family Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies elements of a valid marriage, grounds for divorce and annulment, separation, defenses, custody, support, adoptions, and applicable tax consequences. Includes property settlement agreements, pre- and ante-nuptial agreements, pleadings, and rules of procedure. May include specific federal and Virginia consumer laws.

courses.title: Legal Research
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of various components of a law library, and emphasizes research skills through the use of digests, encyclopedias, reporter systems, codes, citations, ALR, and other research tools. May include research through electronic databases, overview of computer applications, and writing projects.

courses.title: Legal Writing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 or permission of instructor.
courses.description: Studies proper preparation of various legal documents, including legal memoranda, letters, and pleadings. Involves practical applications. May include case and appellate briefs.

courses.title: Law Office Administration and Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces management principles and systems applicable to law firms, including record keeping, disbursements, escrow accounts, billing, and purchasing. May include accounting methods and software packages applicable to law firms.

courses.title: Ethics for the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hour per week.
courses.description: Examines general principles of ethical conduct applicable to paralegals. Includes the application of rules of ethics to the practicing paralegal.

courses.title: Virginia and Federal Procedure
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the rules of procedure in the Virginia and federal court systems, including the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Rules of Practice and Procedure in the District Court, Circuit Court, Court of Appeals, and Supreme Court of Virginia.

courses.title: Torts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of the law of torts and may include preparation and use of pleadings and other documents involved in the trial of a civil action. Emphasizes intentional torts, negligence, personal injury, products liability, and malpractice cases.

courses.title: Trial Preparation and Discovery Practice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the trial process, including the preparation of a trial notebook, pretrial motions, and orders. May include preparation of interrogatories, depositions, and other discovery tools used in assembling evidence in preparation for the trial or an administrative hearing.

courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on major crimes, including their classification, elements of proof, intent, conspiracy, responsibility, parties, and defenses. Emphasizes Virginia law. May include general principles of applicable constitutional law and criminal procedure.

courses.title: Administrative Practice and Procedure
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys applicable administrative laws, including the Privacy Act, the Administrative Process Act, and Freedom of Information Act. Studies practice and procedure involving the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, State Corporation Commission, Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission, Social Security Administration, Virginia Employment Commission, and other administrative agencies.

courses.title: E-Practice
courses.contact_hours: 3 Credits. Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares students to electronically file (e-file) in federal court, state court, and appropriate administrative agencies. Provides the student with the proper information on electronic discovery (e-discovery), including how data are requested, located, and searched in the course of litigation. Focuses on the proper process required to be in conformance with the appropriate laws.

courses.title: Information Technology for the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITE 115 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Provides extensive instruction on the use of technology in the law office, including word processing tools, spreadsheet programs, database management systems, office management programs, case management programs, electronic mail, the cloud, and use of the Internet in the practice of law.

courses.title: Estate Planning and Probate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various devices used to plan an estate, including wills, trust, joint ownership and insurance. Considers various plans in light of family situations and estate objectives. Focuses on practices involving administration of an estate including taxes and preparation of forms.

courses.title: Real Estate Abstracting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews aspects of abstracting title to real estate, recordation of land transactions, liens, grantor-grantee indices, warranties, covenants, restrictions, and easements.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Business Organizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of agency law and the formation of business organizations. Includes sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporation, limited liability companies, and other business entities. Reviews preparation of the documents necessary for the organization and operation of businesses.

courses.title: Bankruptcy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a practical understanding of non-bankruptcy alternatives and the laws of bankruptcy including Chapters 7, 11, 12 and 13 of the Bankruptcy Code. Emphasizes will be placed on preparing petitions, schedules, statements, and other forms.

courses.title: Introduction to Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in arithmetic through introduction to variables and equations.

courses.title: Learning Support for Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 154
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Quantitative Reasoning (MTH 154). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Learning Support for Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 155
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Statistical Reasoning (MTH 155). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in algebra.

courses.title: Learning Support for Pre-Calculus
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 161
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Pre-Calculus (MTH 161). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles, techniques, and vocabulary applicable to all phases of medical laboratory technology.

courses.title: Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, components of health care delivery and clinical laboratory structure. Teaches techniques of specimen collection, specimen handling, and patient interactions.

courses.title: Clinical Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on obtaining blood specimens, processing specimens, managing assignments, assisting with and/or performing specified tests, performing clerical duties and maintaining professional communication. Provides supervised learning in college laboratory/and or cooperating agencies.

courses.title: Urinalysis and Body Fluids
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the gross, chemical, and microscopic techniques used in the clinical laboratory. Emphasizes study of clinical specimens which include the urine, feces, cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and body exudates. Introduces specimen collection and preparation.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the cellular elements of blood including blood cell formation, and routine hematological procedures.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Immunology and Serology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of basic immunology, physiology of the immune system, diseases involving the immune system, as well as serologic procedures.

courses.title: Blood Banking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week..
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of blood grouping and typing, compatibility testing, antibody screening, component preparation, donor selection, and transfusion reactions and investigation.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced study of blood to include coagulation, abnormal bloody formation, and changes seen in various diseases.

courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Molecular Diagnostics
courses.contact_hours: 2 Credits, Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Must be in the final year of the Medical Laboratory Technology AAS degree program or have division approval.
courses.description: Provides the fundamentals of genetics and inheritance along with an overview of the basic principles of clinical molecular diagnostics. Discusses the use of common molecular techniques in the diagnosis of disease.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Labortory 3-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches handling, isolation, and identification of pathogenic microorganisms. Emphasizes clinical techniques of bacteriology, mycology, parasitology and virology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches handling, isolation, and identification of pathogenic microorganisms. Emphasizes clinical techniques of bacteriology, mycology, parasitology and virology. Part II of II.

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry and Instrumentation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 6-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces methods of performing biochemical analysis of clinical specimens. Teaches instrumentation involved in a clinical chemistry laboratory, quality control, and the ability to recognize technical problems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Correlations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Teaches students to apply knowledge gained in courses offered in the MDL curriculum using primarily a case history form of presentation. Emphasizes critical thinking skills in the practice of laboratory medicine.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Mental Health Skill Training I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills necessary to function as a mental health worker, with emphasis on guided practice in counseling skills as well as improved self-awareness. Includes training in problem-solving, goal-setting, and implementation of appropriate strategies and evaluation techniques relating to interaction involving a variety of client needs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Mental Health Skill Training II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops skills necessary to function as a mental health worker, with emphasis on guided practice in counseling skills as well as improved self-awareness. Includes training in problem-solving, goal-setting, and implementation of appropriate strategies and evaluation techniques relating to interaction involving a variety of client needs. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the discipline of marketing and the need to create customer value and relationships in the marketplace. Presents an overview of the marketing principles and management strategies, along with the analytical tools used by organizations in the creation of a marketing plan.

courses.title: Sales and Marketing Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the relationship of professional sales skills and marketing management techniques. Demonstrates the use of the Internet to enhance marketing. Studies legal and ethical considerations.

courses.title: Customer Service Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the role of customer service in achieving a firm's long-term goals; discuses the basic principles of effective customer service; explores the tasks and responsibilities of a customer service manager. Includes such topics as purpose of customer service; establishment of customer service goals and policies; recruitment, selection and training of customer service employees motivation techniques; empowering employees for better decision making; and evaluation of customer service employees and program.

courses.title: Principles of E-Commerce
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies on-line business strategies, and the hardware and software tools necessary for Internet commerce. Includes the identification of appropriate target segments, the development of product opportunities, pricing structures, distribution channels and execution of marketing strategies.

courses.title: Social Media Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Credit Hours: 3, Lecture Hours: 3, Lab Hours: 0, Total Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Surveys the use of social networks and online communities such as blogs, wikis, virtual events that allow companies to expand their interaction with customers and develop relationships with collaborative communities. Emphasizes the ongoing transformation of the way companies adjust their marketing plans to improve interaction with customers online.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Basic Technical Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a foundation in mathematics with emphasis in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry and trigonometry. This course is intended for CTE programs.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents elementary concepts of algebra, linear graphing, financial literacy, descriptive statistics, and measurement & geometry. Based on college programs being supported by this course, colleges may opt to add additional topics such as logic or trigonometry. This course is intended for occupational/technical programs.

courses.title: Technical Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents algebra through unit conversion, trigonometry, vectors, geometry, and complex numbers. This course is intended for CTE programs.

courses.title: Mathematics for Health Professions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents in context the arithmetic of fractions and decimals, the metric system and dimensional analysis, percents, ratio and proportion, linear equations, topics in statistics, topics in geometry, logarithms, topics in health professions including dosages, dilutions and IV flow rates. This course is intended for programs in the Health Professions.

courses.title: Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in proportional reasoning, modeling, financial literacy and validity studies (logic and set theory). Focuses on the process of taking a real-world situation, identifying the mathematical foundation needed to address the problem, solving the problem and applying what is learned to the original situation. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents elementary statistical methods and concepts including visual data presentation, descriptive statistics, probability, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and linear regression. Emphasis is placed on the development of statistical thinking, simulation, and the use of statistical software. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 155 : Statistical Reasoning and MTH 245 : Statistics I or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in power, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, and systems of equations and inequalities. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 161 : Precalculus I and MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: Placement or completion of MTH 161 : Precalculus I or equivalent with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Presents trigonometry, trigonometric applications including Law of Sines and Cosines and an introduction to conics. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 162 : Precalculus II and MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus with Trigonometry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in power, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, systems of equations, trigonometry, and trigonometric applications, including Law of Sines and Cosines, and an introduction to conics. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry and MTH 161 /MTH 162: Precalculus I and II or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Statistics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 154 or MTH 161 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presents an overview of statistics, including descriptive statistics, elementary probability, probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation, and linear regression. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 155 and MTH 245 or equivalent in the same academic plan. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Applied Calculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 161 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduces limits, continuity, differentiation and integration of algebraic, exponential and logarithmic functions, and techniques of integration with an emphasis on applications in business, social sciences and life sciences. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 167 or MTH 161 /162 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presents concepts of limits, derivatives, differentiation of various types of functions and use of differentiation rules, application of differentiation, antiderivatives, integrals and applications of integration. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continues the study of calculus of algebraic and transcendental functions including rectangular, polar, and parametric graphing, indefinite and definite integrals, methods of integration, and power series along with applications. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 : Calculus II or equivalent with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Focuses on extending the concepts of function, limit, continuity, derivative, integral and vector from the plane to the three dimensional space. Covers topics including vector functions, multivariate functions, partial derivatives, multiple integrals and an introduction to vector calculus. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 or equivalent with a grade of B or better or MTH 264 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers matrices, vector spaces, determinants, solutions of systems of linear equations, basis and dimension, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduces ordinary differential equations. Includes first order differential equations, second and higher order ordinary differential equations with applications and numerical methods.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 credits per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 with a grade of C or better or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents topics in sets, counting, graphs, logic, proofs, functions, relations, mathematical induction, Boolean Algebra, and recurrence relations.

courses.title: Music in Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the language of music through an introduction to basic elements, forms and styles across time. Acquaints students with composers' lives and influential creative individualities, discovering representative works and milestones in western society. Develops techniques for listening analytically and critically. Reviews historical development and significance of art music within the context of evolving societal structures. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to Nursing Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 or BIO 231
courses.description: Introduces concepts of nursing practice and conceptual learning.
